screens.name: WOMB ATLAS
screens.purpose:
Observatory Interface

Observe and preserve your experiences, patterns, and health journey.

purpose.ur:
رصد گاہ انٹرفیس

اپنے تجربات، نمونوں اور صحت کے سفر کا مشاہدہ کریں اور محفوظ کریں۔
purpose.fr:
Interface d'observation

Observez et préservez vos expériences, schémas et parcours de santé.
purpose.sw:
Kiolwa cha Uchunguzi

Angalia na uhifadhi uzoefu wako, mitindo, na safari yako ya afya.
purpose.es:
Interfaz del Observatorio

Observa y preserva tus experiencias, patrones y viaje de salud.

screens.name: Consent
screens.purpose:
By continuing, you are creating your first observation within Womb Atlas.

Your information will be handled according to the consent and privacy terms presented throughout the experience.

You may stop at any time.

screens.name: How Womb Atlas Works
screens.purpose:
Womb Atlas does not diagnose conditions or replace medical care.

Your observation is preserved as an Atlas Record, helping you remember, reflect on, and understand patterns over time.

You can skip any question.

screens.name: Quick Safety Check
screens.purpose: Are you currently experiencing any of these?

screens.name: Quick Safety Check
screens.purpose:
SAFETY CHECK

Some of what you selected may need prompt attention.

WOMB ATLAS is not an emergency service.

If symptoms feel severe right now, please consider contacting a healthcare provider, urgent care service, or emergency service.

You can stop or continue later at any time.

Your Safety comes First.

screens.name: Understanding Your Context
screens.purpose:
These questions help provide context for your observation and Atlas Record.

Some sections may adapt based on your responses.
What is your age range?
What best describes your current reproductive stage?
Are you currently using hormonal contraception?

screens.name: Cultural and Language Context
screens.purpose: These next questions help us understand how language, culture, and environment may shape experiences.
Which cultural background(s) best describe you?
What is your current country of residence?
In what country were you born?
What language feels most natural when discussing your health experiences?
Do close family members have a history of the following?

screens.name: Reproductive history
screens.purpose: The next questions are optional and help provide a fuller picture of your reproductive experience over time.
Have you ever been pregnant?
How many pregnancies have you had?
Have you experienced pregnancy loss?
Have you ever tried to become pregnant for 12 months or longer without becoming pregnant?

screens.purpose: The next questions are about bleeding patterns and experiences, if they apply to you.

screens.purpose: The next questions are about pain, discomfort, and how symptoms affect your body over time.

When does the pain typically occur?

screens.purpose: The next questions are about cycle patterns, body rhythms, and hormonal changes over time.
How predictable are your cycles?

screens.name: Daily life and impact
screens.purpose: The next questions ask about energy, fatigue, and how symptoms affect daily life over time.
During your period or symptoms, how often do you miss work, school, or other activities?
How often do you feel unusually tired or fatigued?
Have your symptoms ever disrupted your sleep?
Do you feel dizzy or faint during your period?
How often does this level of impact happen?
Which areas of your life are most affected by your symptoms?
Even if this feels normal to you, does it ever stop you from doing things you want to do?
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
Overall, your symptoms are:

screens.name: Care and support
screens.purpose: The next questions ask about experiences seeking care, support, or answers.
Have you spoken to a healthcare provider about these symptoms?
What was that experience like?
Have you ever felt your symptoms were dismissed, ignored, or explained away?
Do you currently feel you have access to care or support if you need it?

screens.name: In your own words
screens.purpose:
The next questions give you space to describe what has been happening in your own way.

You can type, record your voice, or leave any field blank.

You do not need to use medical words.

screens.name: Narrative complete
screens.purpose:
Some experiences are more personal to describe.

The next questions are optional, and you may skip any part of them.

Your responses help the observatory understand patterns more carefully, but you remain in control of what you share.

screens.name: Sensitive topics
screens.purpose:
Some experiences are more personal to describe.

The next questions are optional, and you may skip any part of them.

Your responses help the observatory understand patterns more carefully, but you remain in control of what you share.
Do you experience pain during sex?
Have you experienced pain or discomfort during bowel movements?
Have you noticed unusual discharge, odor, or changes that concerned you?
Which part of your experience feels most important to you right now?

screens.name: Thank you.
screens.purpose:
You've completed the personal questions section.

The next step is reviewing your responses before creating your reflection summary.

Your responses remain private and are intended to support reflection, not diagnosis.
Preparing your Atlas Record...

screens.name: Reflection summary
screens.purpose: You may return to any section before creating your reflection summary.

screens.name: Ready to continue?
screens.purpose:
Atlas is organizing your responses by identifying observed experiences, looking for recurring patterns, and connecting experiences that may be related.

It will create a safe, non-diagnostic reflection that focuses on body literacy and keeps your own experience at the center.

This will build your first Atlas Record, a private starting point for noticing what remains stable, what changes, and what becomes clearer over time.

screens.name: Creating your reflection summary
screens.purpose: This may take a few moments. Please stay with us.

screens.name: Your Atlas Record has been saved.
screens.purpose:
Thank you for sharing your experience.

Your story has been added to your private Atlas Timeline.

Continue your journey

Future observations will help Atlas understand what remains stable, what changes, what becomes clearer, and what patterns emerge over time.

screens.name: Creating Observational Record
screens.purpose:
This may take a few moments.

Please stay with us.

screens.name: Constellation Record
screens.purpose: A visual map of the observed patterns Atlas noticed in this first record.

screens.name: Observed Patterns
screens.purpose: These pattern cards organize what you shared into plain-language, body-literacy reflections.

screens.name: ATLAS RECORD
screens.purpose: A baseline portrait of what you shared today.

screens.name: Atlas Check-In Landing
screens.purpose: Invite returning participant to update their observation.

screens.name: Check-In Reason
screens.purpose: Capture why participant is returning.

screens.name: Symptom Change Check
screens.purpose: Capture whether symptoms changed since previous record.

screens.name: Bleeding Change Check
screens.purpose: Capture bleeding changes since last record.

screens.name: Pain Change Check
screens.purpose: Capture pain changes since last record.

screens.name: Care Update
screens.purpose: Capture care-seeking or support changes.

screens.name: New Narrative
screens.purpose: Capture short update in participant's own words.

screens.name: Check-In Review
screens.purpose: Review updates before saving.

screens.name: Updated Atlas Record
screens.purpose: Show changes against prior Atlas Record.

screens.name: Check-In Saved
screens.purpose: Confirm check-in is saved to participant record.
